answer.evidence: The cliff and stairs section (rows 0-15) is drawn as two stacked steps. Row 0 is a light edge and rows 1-4 are the tread. Row 5 (L=145) is a lighter edge line above a dark shadow at rows 6-7 (L=99, then L=63), which is the riser. A second light tread starts at row 8 (L=197) and runs through rows 9-10, followed by a face with shadow at rows 11-14. Row 15 is a dark base line. Below it, rows 16-31 are a flat top-down cobble ground texture with no edge, which is normal for terrain. The grass and dirt strips at the left and right edges (x 0-7 and 40-47) are side caps. The steps show treads with edge lines and shadow plus risers, so they read as three-quarter and not as a flat front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small strip: a grass lip on top, two wooden posts, and a stone step face of horizontal bands. It has only 14 distinct colours in total, against 80 for the grass reference. Its 6 visible tones per tile are close to the paving reference (7) and above the grass reference (3), and it has no large flat areas (0% near-flat). The structure is shallow, though. The stone bands are mostly smooth with few per-stone highlights or grain, unlike the paving reference, where stones are shaded one by one. The wood posts and grass edge have only 2-3 steps each. About 41% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is partly near-black, partly tinted. Side by side it reads thinner and more sticker-like than the references, and it does not clearly reach the Beodeul bar. When in doubt, fail.
